q: Look at the following sets of pictures. Put them in the right order so that they will tell a story. [Six numbered cartoon panels: 1 - mother and child together in the lit kitchen, child eating; 2 - dark bedroom, child sitting up in bed eating, 'CHOMP! CHOMP!'; 3 - kitchen, child alone on tiptoe at the counter eating; 4 - dark bedroom, child asleep with a dream bubble showing a monstrous figure; 5 - mother tucking the child into bed, bedside lamp lit; 6 - dark bedroom, child sitting up reaching towards the bedside table.]
exp: The nightmare panel is the consequence and so belongs last, and the eating-in-bed panel must come immediately before it, which rules out the orders that place the dream in the middle or end on a kitchen scene. That leaves the reading: snack with mother, tucked in, sneaks back to the kitchen, sits up in bed, eats, bad dream. The alternative order 1 5 6 2 4 3 is also arguable if the lit kitchen panel is meant as the next morning, so this is a genuine judgement call and the printed panels are needed.

sitting: Computer Operator (CB) under Mizoram Information Commission, 2016 - Paper II
q: In this test, parts of a well known object are placed in the wrong order. You have to choose the correct order, from left to right, in which these parts should be placed in order to form the object. The parts of each object are numbered. [Six black silhouette fragments of an animal: 1 - slab with a horn/ear spur on top and a foreleg below; 2 - plain torso slab with one leg; 3 - hindquarters with a straight hind leg and a second hind leg bent back at the hock; 4 - head with horns and a muzzle facing right; 5 - large torso block with a raised back and one leg; 6 - narrow slab with a tufted lower edge.]
exp: The object is a cow facing right: fragment 4 is the horned head with the muzzle on the right and a straight cut on its left, so it goes last, and fragment 3 carries the bent hind leg, so it goes first. Fragment 1 has the second horn spur on its upper edge, which forces it next to the head - reassembling the fragments in this order produces a continuous cow silhouette, whereas the other orders leave a horn standing up in the middle of the animal's back. The printed fragments are needed to confirm.
